sections.h2: Where is the Harnett County Register of Deeds and what does it record?
sections.html:
The office is at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 200, Lillington, NC 27546, and it records deeds, deeds of trust, maps and plats, powers of attorney and UCC filings for the county. North Carolina voters elect the register of deeds every two years under G.S. 161-1.

Everything on file is public record except military discharges. Harnett County was carved out of Cumberland County in 1855, and the office holds records back to that year, though fires in 1892 and 1894 destroyed many early ones.

Staff are barred by statute from running title searches, so a buyer or seller who wants a chain of title needs a closing attorney or title company. Records are indexed by name rather than address. To find an owner by address, the office points people to the county GIS viewer.

sections.h2: What are the Harnett County recording fees?
sections.html:
A deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each extra page, and a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 per added page. These figures come from the uniform fee schedule the county posted with a July 1, 2026 effective date, and they match G.S. 161-10.

Source: Harnett County Register of Deeds uniform fee schedule. The schedule also notes that satisfactions of a deed of trust cost nothing to record, which helps a seller whose payoff is being cleared at closing.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Harnett County deed?
sections.html:
The excise tax on a conveyance is $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, or a fraction of $500, and the county prints it as $2.00 per $1,000. It has been at that rate for deeds since August 1, 1991, according to the register's history table.

The transferor, usually the seller, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. Under G.S. 105-228.30, half goes to the county general fund and half is sent to the state Department of Revenue after a small county allowance.

The county page lists the earlier rates as well, from a 50-cent rate in 1968 to the current one. Ask the closing attorney to show the excise tax as its own line on the seller side of the settlement statement.

sections.h2: When does a deed count as recorded in Harnett County?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded when the office keys it into the system, and the register's own cutoffs decide which day that is. Walk-in customers have no fixed cutoff, but a document that cannot be keyed before 5:00 p.m. rolls to the next business day, and e-recording closes at 4:45 p.m.

The time matters because priority follows the order of registration. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal is not valid against lien creditors or buyers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies.

  • Electronic recording is open for every document type, including maps and plats.
  • Maps must be 24x36 or 18x24 inches, the only two sizes accepted.
  • Mailed requests for copies go to the Suite 200 address, and certified copies of real estate documents are handled by contacting the office.

sections.h2: What should a Harnett County seller check before the deed is signed?
sections.html:
Confirm that the name on the deed matches the owner of record, because the register cannot add or remove names from a deed. A name change needs a new deed, and the office suggests an attorney unless the owner is familiar with drafting legal documents.

  • Search the grantor index by owner name for open deeds of trust, then ask the lender for a payoff.
  • Look for a recorded power of attorney if someone else is signing. The office records powers of attorney but not healthcare ones.
  • For an inherited house, check whether the estate paperwork is on file with the clerk of court, since divorce and estate records are kept there rather than at the register.
  • Pull the unpaid-tax balance from the Tax Department, which is at Suite 101 on the same street address.

Separation agreements show up at the register only if they were recorded. A seller going through a separation should ask whether one exists and whether it touches the house.

sections.h2: How do I get a copy of a Harnett County record?
sections.html:
Copies can be requested in person, by mail to the Suite 200 address, or through the county's online record search. Uncertified copies cost $0.25 each on the posted schedule, and certified copies cost $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.

Because the index is by name, searches work best with the exact spelling used on the deed. Try the seller's name, a spouse's name and a former trust or company name. For an older chain of title, remember that the early books were hit by the 1892 and 1894 fires, so a closing attorney may need to work from later instruments.

Other filings handled by the office include assumed business names, which cost $26.00 to record on paper or $41.00 online, and fixture filings under the UCC. Neither affects a house sale unless the property secures a business loan.

sections.h2: Who records a deed after a Harnett County tax foreclosure sale?
sections.html:
The buyer does. When a Harnett County tax foreclosure sale is confirmed, the buyer receives a commissioner's deed, and the county's foreclosure page puts the duty to record it with the register of deeds on that buyer as soon as possible.

The same page says all properties sell as is, with no warranty from the county or the commissioner, and sales are not subject to financing or marketable title. An owner facing that process can redeem before confirmation or sell the house to a buyer who closes first, with the deed recorded here like any other.

sections.h2: What does Harnett County look like for a house sale?
sections.html:
Census Bureau figures describe the people a seller in Harnett County is marketing to. These are the ones most tied to housing.

  • Households for 2020-2024: 49,845, averaging 2.73 persons each.
  • Residents 65 and over: 14.7%, and veterans number 11,660.
  • Median gross rent: $1,112, with median owner costs of $1,594 a month for owners with a mortgage.
  • Living in the same house one year earlier: 86.8% of residents aged one and over.
  • Land area: 594.93 square miles, or about 224.5 people per square mile in 2020 (Census QuickFacts).

Workers in the county average 32.8 minutes of travel to work, a figure buyers weigh against the price of a house.

faqs.q: What is the Harnett County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: A deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for every page after that. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages. Those are the figures on the schedule dated July 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Harnett County deed?
faqs.a: The seller, as the transferor, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The rate is $1.00 per $500 of the consideration or value.

faqs.q: Can the Harnett County Register of Deeds search my title?
faqs.a: No. State law bars register staff from performing title searches. An attorney, a title company or the owner can search the records, which are indexed by name, and the GIS viewer helps match a name to an address.

faqs.q: What time must a deed arrive in Harnett County to be recorded the same day?
faqs.a: In person, it must be keyed before 5:00 p.m., and that depends on how long the document takes to enter. E-recordings must arrive by 4:45 p.m. Anything later is recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: Is a satisfaction of mortgage recorded for free in Harnett County?
faqs.a: Yes. The uniform fee schedule lists satisfactions and cancellations of deeds of trust at no charge. The lender records the satisfaction after the loan is paid off.
